questions.question: In a motor vehicle on a highway, is it legal to drink or carry open alcohol containers?

options.text: No. It is illegal to drink from or carry open alcohol containers.
Yes, if you are not driving.
Yes, if you are driving but not drunk.

questions.correctAnswerText: No. It is illegal to drink from or carry open alcohol containers.
questions.explanation: It is illegal to drive while under the influence of alcohol. Drivers and passengers cannot have open alcohol containers in a moving vehicle.

questions.question: When crossing a sidewalk to enter traffic from an alley or driveway, what should you do?

options.text: Stop only if you see pedestrians on the sidewalk.
Stop before driving onto the sidewalk.
Expect pedestrians to move out of your way.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop before driving onto the sidewalk.
questions.explanation: You must stop before driving onto a sidewalk when leaving an alley, driveway, or parking lot. Pedestrians and other traffic have the right-of-way.

questions.question: What should you do if someone is following you too closely on a two-lane road?

options.text: Slowly reduce your speed to let them drive around you.
Speed up to increase the distance between you.
Tap your brakes to slow down, then speed back up.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slowly reduce your speed to let them drive around you.
questions.explanation: If someone is tailgating you, try to move to another lane. If you cannot change lanes, slowly reduce your speed when it is safe. This encourages the tailgater to pass you.

questions.question: If an oncoming driver does not dim their headlights, where should you look?

options.text: At the center of the road.
Toward the right side of the road.
Straight ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Toward the right side of the road.
questions.explanation: Look toward the right side of the road to avoid being blinded by bright headlights. This lets you see enough of the road to stay on course. Do not shine your bright lights back at them.

questions.question: When parking uphill on a road with a curb, which way should your front wheels point?

options.text: Toward the curb.
Away from the curb.
Straight ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Away from the curb.
questions.explanation: Turn your wheels away from the curb when parking uphill. If your brakes fail and your car rolls backward, it will roll away from traffic.

questions.question: When merging onto the freeway, how fast should you drive?

options.text: At or near the speed of freeway traffic.
5 to 10 mph slower than freeway traffic.
The posted speed limit.

questions.correctAnswerText: At or near the speed of freeway traffic.
questions.explanation: Merge onto the freeway at or near the speed of traffic already on the freeway.

questions.question: What should you do as you approach the top of a hill?

options.text: Speed up slightly.
Be ready to stop if needed.
Keep the same speed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be ready to stop if needed.
questions.explanation: You cannot see what is beyond a hill or around a curve. A vehicle might be stopped just out of sight. Always slow down near hills and curves so you can stop if necessary.

questions.question: What does a broken yellow centerline mean?

options.text: You cannot pass.
You can pass on the right when it is safe.
You can pass on the left when it is safe.

questions.correctAnswerText: You can pass on the left when it is safe.
questions.explanation: A broken yellow line on your side means you can cross it to pass on the left when the road ahead is clear.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Railroad crossing.
Warning.
Traffic signal ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Warning.
questions.explanation: A yellow diamond-shaped sign warns you of danger ahead. Orange diamond signs warn of dangers in or near work zones.

questions.question: When a school bus is picking up or dropping off children, what must you do?

options.text: Stop, no matter which direction you are driving.
Stop only if you are driving in the same direction.
Slow down and be ready to stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop, no matter which direction you are driving.
questions.explanation: You must come to a complete stop before reaching a school bus that is picking up or dropping off children, regardless of which direction you are traveling.

questions.question: When should you increase the distance between your vehicle and the vehicle ahead?

options.text: When you are following a small passenger vehicle.
When another driver is tailgating you.
When you are driving slower than the posted speed limit.

questions.correctAnswerText: When another driver is tailgating you.
questions.explanation: When being tailgated, give yourself extra space in front of your vehicle. Slow down gradually or change lanes to avoid a collision. Do not brake suddenly.

questions.question: If you are about to be hit from behind, which action should you NOT do?

options.text: Apply your brakes.
Let go of the steering wheel.
Press your head firmly against the head restraint.

questions.correctAnswerText: Let go of the steering wheel.
questions.explanation: If hit from behind, press yourself against your seat and hold your head against the head restraint to prevent whiplash. Keep a firm grip on the steering wheel and be ready to brake to avoid hitting the vehicle in front of you.

questions.question: What does a flashing red light mean?

options.text: You are traveling in the wrong direction.
Treat the intersection like a stop sign.
You cannot proceed until the light turns green.

questions.correctAnswerText: Treat the intersection like a stop sign.
questions.explanation: A flashing red light works like a stop sign. Come to a complete stop before the crosswalk or stop line. Yield to all other traffic and pedestrians before proceeding.

questions.question: When passing another vehicle, you should:

options.text: Not assume other drivers will make room for you to return to your lane.
Assume other drivers will let you pass if you signal.
Assume other drivers will maintain the same speed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Not assume other drivers will make room for you to return to your lane.
questions.explanation: Even when you signal, do not assume that other drivers will give you space or the right-of-way.

questions.question: If your tires lose contact with the road surface, you should:

options.text: Slow down by shifting into a lower gear.
Ease your foot off the gas pedal.
Slow down by pumping the brakes quickly and firmly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ease your foot off the gas pedal.
questions.explanation: If your tires lose grip, ease off the gas pedal and avoid using the brakes. Wait until your tires grip the road again before steering or stopping.

questions.question: A driver license is a:

options.text: Right, not a privilege.
Privilege, not a right.
Requirement.

questions.correctAnswerText: Privilege, not a right.
questions.explanation: A driver license is a privilege that must be earned and kept. It is not a right.

questions.question: In bad weather, you should:

options.text: Steer off the road.
Drive in a low gear.
Steer and brake smoothly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Steer and brake smoothly.
questions.explanation: In bad weather, avoid hard braking and sharp turns. These actions make it harder to control your vehicle.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: No right turn.
Stop sign ahead.
Divided highway.

questions.correctAnswerText: No right turn.
questions.explanation: This sign means you cannot turn in the direction the arrow points. In this case, right turns are not allowed.

questions.question: What do broken yellow lines mean?

options.text: No passing is allowed.
They separate traffic moving in the same direction.
They separate traffic moving in opposite directions.

questions.correctAnswerText: They separate traffic moving in opposite directions.
questions.explanation: Yellow lines separate traffic moving in opposite directions. Broken lines mean you can pass when it is safe to do so.

questions.question: When passing another vehicle, when should you return to your original lane?

options.text: When you can see both headlights of the other vehicle in your rearview mirror.
When you have cleared the front bumper of the other vehicle.
When you are 50 feet in front of the other vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: When you can see both headlights of the other vehicle in your rearview mirror.
questions.explanation: Return to your lane only when you can see both headlights of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror. This ensures you have enough safe distance ahead.

questions.question: How do you make room for cars entering the freeway?

options.text: Slow down.
Move to a different lane.
Keep your speed and position the same.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move to a different lane.
questions.explanation: Make room for vehicles entering the freeway. If you can, move to the next lane to create a gap. If you cannot move lanes, slow down to let the incoming vehicles enter traffic safely.

questions.question: You are in the left lane of two lanes going your direction. Many cars are passing you on the right. A driver behind you wants to go faster. What should you do?

options.text: Stay in your lane so traffic flows smoothly.
Drive onto the left shoulder to let cars pass.
Move to the right lane when it is safe.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move to the right lane when it is safe.
questions.explanation: Use the left lane to drive fast, pass, or turn left. Use the right lane when driving slower than traffic, entering the road, or turning right.

questions.question: What speed should you always travel at?

options.text: The same speed as surrounding vehicles.
The speed limit.
A speed that fits the road and weather conditions.

questions.correctAnswerText: A speed that fits the road and weather conditions.
questions.explanation: Your speed depends on road conditions, weather, and the legal speed limit. Never drive faster than the speed limit. Slow down when conditions are not ideal.

questions.question: Your vehicle has an Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS). You need to stop quickly. What should you do?

options.text: Press the brake pedal hard and hold it down.
Pump the brake pedal.
Press the brake pedal slowly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Press the brake pedal hard and hold it down.
questions.explanation: With ABS, press the brake pedal as hard as you can and keep it pressed. The ABS will pump the brakes automatically. Do not release the brake pedal. ABS only works when the brake pedal is fully pressed.

questions.question: You want to enter the freeway but you don't see a gap in traffic. What should you do?

options.text: Keep your speed and force other drivers to make a gap.
Slow down on the ramp and wait for a gap.
Stop at the end of the ramp and wait for a gap.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down on the ramp and wait for a gap.
questions.explanation: If you don't see a gap in traffic, slow down on the ramp. Do not stop at the end of the ramp because you won't have enough space to speed up and match traffic before entering.
